overall: Atlanta is tracking warmer than model guidance on this sunny, breezy afternoon, with a running max of 84.2°F as of 14:15 ET already exceeding all NWP model forecasts. NW winds around 17 mph and a relatively low dewpoint (64.4°F) reflect a dry, post-frontal airmass, which is limiting moisture but not heat gain. The active NWS alerts (thunderstorms near Pelham/Moody AFB and Satilla River flooding) are confined to south and southeast Georgia, well away from Atlanta, and pose no direct impact on today's TMAX.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF 82.3°F, HRRR 82.6°F, NBM 82.6°F) and the NWS point forecast (near 83°F) have already been surpassed by 14:15 ET, indicating a notable warm bias in today's model guidance. The timing spread is wide (ECMWF/HRRR peaking at 10h vs. NBM at 20h), but the intraday timing model and observed hour-of-max (13:19 ET) suggest the peak is near or just past, though velocity remains slightly positive at +1.5°F/hr.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 84.2°F, persistent positive velocity (+1.5°F/hr) and positive acceleration, there is meaningful potential for modest additional warming before sunset; the META model places 46.1% probability on 84–85°F and 29.5% on 86–87°F, yielding a probability-weighted estimate near 85.5°F. The scattered cloud cover (38%), dry airmass, and proximity to the diurnal peak together suggest the high will settle in the 85–86°F range, modestly above the NWS and NWP guidance. Confidence is moderate — the day's peak is likely close but not definitively past.
